messages.content: Build a tiny Pong game in one HTML file. Use canvas, keyboard controls, scoring, and a simple computer opponent.

Save as pong.html and open it directly. It is complete and dependency-free:

```html
<!doctype html><canvas id=c width=640 height=360></canvas><script>const c=document.querySelector('canvas'),x=c.getContext('2d');let p=150,b={x:320,y:180,vx:4,vy:3},s=[0,0];onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='ArrowUp')p-=20;if(e.key==='ArrowDown')p+=20};function f(){x.fillStyle='#111';x.fillRect(0,0,640,360);p=Math.max(0,Math.min(300,p));x.fillStyle='white';x.fillRect(20,p,10,60);x.fillRect(610,b.y-30,10,60);x.fillRect(b.x-6,b.y-6,12,12);x.font='28px sans-serif';x.fillText(s.join(' : '),290,35);b.x+=b.vx;b.y+=b.vy;if(b.y<6||b.y>354)b.vy*=-1;if(b.x<30&&b.y>p&&b.y<p+60)b.vx=Math.abs(b.vx);if(b.x>600&&b.y>b.y-30&&b.y< b.y+30)b.vx=-Math.abs(b.vx);if(b.x<0){s[1]++;b={x:320,y:180,vx:4,vy:3}}if(b.x>640){s[0]++;b={x:320,y:180,vx:-4,vy:3}}requestAnimationFrame(f)}f()</script>
```
Use the arrow keys to move the left paddle.
Add W/S controls and a pause key.
Create a standalone Breakout game with canvas, bricks, paddle, lives, and restart.

Here is a runnable single file, breakout.html:

```html
<!doctype html><canvas id=c width=600 height=400></canvas><script>let c=document.querySelector('canvas'),g=c.getContext('2d'),x=280,b={x:300,y:350,vx:3,vy:-3},l=3,a=Array.from({length:30},(_,i)=>({x:i%10*60,y:30+(i/10|0)*22,on:1}));onmousemove=e=>x=e.clientX-c.offsetLeft-45;function f(){g.fillStyle='#18202b';g.fillRect(0,0,600,400);g.fillStyle='#f55';a.forEach(q=>q.on&&g.fillRect(q.x+1,q.y+1,58,20));g.fillStyle='#5cf';g.fillRect(x,370,90,12);g.fillStyle='white';g.beginPath();g.arc(b.x,b.y,7,0,7);g.fill();b.x+=b.vx;b.y+=b.vy;if(b.x<7||b.x>593)b.vx*=-1;if(b.y<7)b.vy*=-1;if(b.y>360&&b.x>x&&b.x<x+90)b.vy=-Math.abs(b.vy);a.forEach(q=>{if(q.on&&b.x>q.x&&b.x<q.x+60&&b.y>q.y&&b.y<q.y+22){q.on=0;b.vy*=-1}});if(b.y>410){l--;b={x:300,y:350,vx:3,vy:-3}};g.fillText('Lives: '+l,10,395);requestAnimationFrame(f)}f()</script>
```
Move the paddle with the mouse; clear every brick or lose three lives.
Make the paddle follow arrow keys too and show a win message.

Add `let keys={};onkeydown=e=>keys[e.key]=1;onkeyup=e=>keys[e.key]=0;` and at the start of `f()` add `x+=((keys.ArrowRight||0)-(keys.ArrowLeft||0))*7;x=Math.max(0,Math.min(510,x));`. Before scheduling the next frame, add `if(!a.some(q=>q.on)){g.fillText('YOU WIN! Press R to replay',220,220);return}` and `onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='r')location.reload();keys[e.key]=1}`.
Make a one-file clicker game with a score, upgrade button, and automatic income.

Save this as clicker.html and open it: ```html

``` It works without a server and upgrades both click power and passive income.
Add a reset button and save progress in localStorage.

Add `<button id=reset>Reset</button>` and replace the state declaration with `let z=JSON.parse(localStorage.game||'null')||{score:0,power:1,cost:10,auto:0};let {score,power,cost,auto}=z;`. At the end of `draw`, add `localStorage.game=JSON.stringify({score,power,cost,auto})`. Finally add `reset.onclick=()=>{localStorage.removeItem('game');location.reload()}`.
Build a tic-tac-toe game in one HTML file for two local players, with win detection.

Use this complete tic.html: ```html

``` Players click empty squares; the board stops after a win or draw.
Add a New Game button and highlight the winning cells.
Add a New Game button and highlight each winning index with a gold background. Set the button handler to reload the page for a fresh board.
Create a reaction-time game in one self-contained HTML file with a start button and best score.

Save as reaction.html: ```html
Click Start

``` Click only when the panel turns green; clicking early does not falsely award a score.
Track three rounds and report the average.

Add `let times=[];` beside the existing state. In the click handler, after `let ms=...`, use `times.push(ms);msg.textContent=times.length<3?`${ms} ms — round ${times.length}/3`:`Average ${Math.round(times.reduce((a,v)=>a+v,0)/3)} ms`;if(times.length===3)start.disabled=1;`. Reset `times=[]` when starting a new session if desired.
Build a small multiple-choice quiz game in one HTML file with score and next-question flow.

This quiz.html is complete and runnable: ```html

``` Each answer immediately advances, and the final score is shown.
Shuffle the choices while keeping the correct answer working.

In `show()`, replace the choices rendering with `let opts=data[i][1].map((text,j)=>({text,ok:j===data[i][2]})).sort(()=>Math.random()-.5);choices.innerHTML=opts.map((o,j)=>`<button onclick='pick(${j},${o.ok})'>${o.text}</button>`).join('')`. Change `function pick(j){` to `function pick(j,ok){` and increment with `if(ok)score++`.
Make a memory matching game in a single HTML file with shuffled emoji cards and move count.

Save as memory.html: ```html

``` Cards stay matched and mismatches flip back after a short delay.
Add a completion message when every pair is matched.
Add `let matched=0;` to the state. In the matching branch, use `matched++;open=[];if(matched===4)info.textContent='Complete in '+moves+' moves!'`; keep the mismatch timeout unchanged.
Create a canvas dodging game where the player avoids falling blocks, with score and game-over restart.

Here is dodge.html, a complete standalone game:

```html
<!doctype html><canvas id=c width=360 height=500></canvas><script>let g=c.getContext('2d'),p=165,y=450,obs=[],score=0,dead=0;onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='ArrowLeft')p-=18;if(e.key==='ArrowRight')p+=18;if(dead&&e.key==='r')location.reload()};function f(){g.fillStyle='#101820';g.fillRect(0,0,360,500);p=Math.max(0,Math.min(310,p));if(Math.random()<.03)obs.push({x:Math.random()*330,y:-20});g.fillStyle='#5cf';g.fillRect(p,y,50,15);g.fillStyle='#f66';obs.forEach(o=>{o.y+=4;g.fillRect(o.x,o.y,30,20);if(o.x<p+50&&o.x+30>p&&o.y<y+15&&o.y+20>y)dead=1});obs=obs.filter(o=>o.y<510);g.fillStyle='white';g.fillText(dead?'GAME OVER - R to restart':'Score '+(++score),10,20);if(!dead)requestAnimationFrame(f)}f()</script>
```
Use left and right arrows to survive as long as possible.
Add touch buttons for phones.

Add `<button onclick='p-=25'>◀</button><button onclick='p+=25'>▶</button>` after the canvas. Clamp `p` in the frame as already shown; the buttons now provide mobile controls while keyboard controls remain available.
Build a one-file Whack-a-Mole game with a 3x3 grid, timer, and score.

Save as mole.html and open it: ```html

``` Click the mole before it moves; the round lasts 20 seconds.
Add a Start button so the timer does not begin until the player is ready.

Put `<button id=start>Start</button>` before the grid and wrap the existing timer setup in `start.onclick=()=>{start.disabled=true;let timer=setInterval(()=>{...},1000)}`. Keep `hit` outside so it can read the current `mole`; initialize `mole=-1` as before.
Make a keyboard-controlled maze game in one HTML file where a square reaches a goal.

This maze.html is runnable with no assets:

```html
<!doctype html><canvas id=c width=300 height=300></canvas><script>let x=20,y=20,g=c.getContext('2d'),walls=[[60,0,10,230],[120,70,10,230],[180,0,10,230],[240,70,10,230]];onkeydown=e=>{let dx=(e.key==='ArrowRight')*10-(e.key==='ArrowLeft')*10,dy=(e.key==='ArrowDown')*10-(e.key==='ArrowUp')*10,nx=x+dx,ny=y+dy;if(nx>=0&&ny>=0&&nx<280&&ny<280&&!walls.some(w=>nx<w[0]+w[2]&&nx+20>w[0]&&ny<w[1]+w[3]&&ny+20>w[1]))[x,y]=[nx,ny];draw()};function draw(){g.fillStyle='white';g.fillRect(0,0,300,300);g.fillStyle='black';walls.forEach(w=>g.fillRect(...w));g.fillStyle='lime';g.fillRect(260,260,20,20);g.fillStyle='blue';g.fillRect(x,y,20,20);if(x>240&&y>240)g.fillText('YOU WIN',120,150)}draw()</script>
```
Arrow keys move the blue square through the corridors to the green goal.
Add a move counter and reset key.

Add `let moves=0;` to the state, increment it immediately before `draw()` with `moves++`, and draw `g.fillText('Moves: '+moves,8,15)` at the end of `draw()`. Add `if(e.key==='r'){x=20;y=20;moves=0;draw();return}` at the top of the key handler.
Create a Simon-style color memory game in one standalone HTML file.

Save as simon.html: ```html

``` The sequence grows after each correct round; click colors in order.
Flash each color in the sequence instead of displaying the answer text.

In `next()`, replace the text assignment with `let i=0,show=()=>{if(i===seq.length)return m.textContent='Your turn';let e=[...b.children][colors.indexOf(seq[i++])];e.style.opacity=.3;setTimeout(()=>{e.style.opacity=1;setTimeout(show,200)},400)};show()`. Keep `tap` disabled during playback by adding a `watching` flag if you need strict timing.
Build a hangman word game as one HTML file with guessed letters and limited misses.

Here is hangman.html: ```html

``` Enter one letter at a time; duplicate guesses are ignored.
Add a new random word button.

Define `let words=['JAVASCRIPT','BROWSER','CANVAS','PUZZLE'];` and change the state to `let word=words[Math.random()*words.length|0],used=[],miss=0`. Add `<button onclick='location.reload()'>New word</button>` after the message. The reload chooses a fresh word.
Make a one-file number guessing game with hints, attempts, and a replay button.

Save this as guess.html: ```html

Guess 1–100

``` The hint updates after each attempt and the target remains hidden until success.
Add a best-score counter using localStorage.

At the top add `let best=+localStorage.best||Infinity;`. In the correct branch, set `best=Math.min(best,tries);localStorage.best=best;m.textContent+=` Best: ${best}``. This persists the fewest attempts across reloads.
Create a simple Frogger-like crossing game in one HTML file with lanes and moving cars.

This cross.html runs directly:

```html
<!doctype html><canvas id=c width=360 height=360></canvas><script>let g=c.getContext('2d'),x=170,y=330,cars=[0,100,220];onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='ArrowUp')y-=30;if(e.key==='ArrowDown')y+=30;if(e.key==='ArrowLeft')x-=30;if(e.key==='ArrowRight')x+=30};function f(){g.fillStyle='#174';g.fillRect(0,0,360,360);g.fillStyle='#444';g.fillRect(0,60,360,240);g.fillStyle='orange';cars=cars.map((v,i)=>(v+2+i)%380);cars.forEach((v,i)=>g.fillRect(v-20,90+i*60,40,25));g.fillStyle='yellow';g.fillRect(x,y,20,20);if(cars.some((v,i)=>Math.abs(v-x)<30&&Math.abs(y-(90+i*60))<25))location.reload();if(y<30){g.fillText('SAFE!',155,30);return}requestAnimationFrame(f)}f()</script>
```
Guide the yellow player upward; touching a car restarts the game.
Add a score for each successful crossing and a high-score display.

Add `let score=0,best=+localStorage.crossBest||0;` and when `y<30`, run `score++;best=Math.max(best,score);localStorage.crossBest=best;y=330;x=170`. Draw `g.fillText('Score '+score+' Best '+best,8,18)` each frame. This lets the player make repeated crossings.
Build a tiny typing speed game in one HTML file that shows a word and measures completion time.

Save as typing.html: ```html

``` Type each displayed word exactly; the timer resets per word and reports completion.
Add a words-per-minute result and a restart button.

Track `let totalStart=performance.now()` separately from the per-word `start`. On completion calculate `let minutes=(performance.now()-totalStart)/60000;msg.textContent+=' WPM: '+Math.round(words.length/minutes/5)`. Add `<button onclick='location.reload()'>Restart</button>` beside the input.
